subject: roundabout town traffic
title: What If a Town Removed Its Traffic Lights? A Dutch One Did, and Crashes Fell

scenes.text: What if a town switched off its traffic lights? One did. Crashes dropped.
Drachten, in the Netherlands, 50,000 people. Engineer Hans Monderman pulled out 12 of its 15 traffic lights and most of its road signs.
His rule: when you treat people like idiots, they behave like idiots. Take the signs away and drivers start looking at each other instead.
At one junction handling 22,000 cars a day, the lights became a roundabout. Thirty-six crashes in the four years before. Two in the two years after.
Traffic moved more briskly, tailbacks and road rage faded, and the town went years without a single traffic death.
The idea is called shared space. It works because nobody is sure who has right of way, so everybody slows down and makes eye contact.

description:
What if a town removed its traffic lights? Drachten, a Dutch town of about 50,000 people, took out 12 of its 15 traffic lights and most of its road signs under engineer Hans Monderman's shared space approach.
At one intersection handling about 22,000 cars a day, the signals were replaced by a roundabout; the junction saw 36 crashes in the four years before and just two in the two years after. Traffic moved more briskly, backups and road rage largely vanished, and the town recorded no traffic deaths for years. Monderman's explanation: when drivers are unsure who has right of way, they slow down and seek eye contact.
